title: Procedural projects: from Townscaper to living worlds
scope: A discovery collection, not new canonical component manifests. Existing components are referenced by ID. Candidate projects are not yet integrated into the main explorer, package or MCP.

projects.name: Townscaper
projects.summary: Interactive town-building toy: coloured blocks on an irregular grid become houses, arches, stairs and bridges.
projects.study: Minimal input, automatic architectural detail and immediate feedback.
projects.boundary: Product inspiration, not a reusable engine or a grant to copy code or assets. Exact internal implementation is not inferred from appearance.

projects.name: Tiny Glade
projects.summary: Gridless building toy in which walls, paths and raised structures receive context-sensitive architectural detail.
projects.study: Continuous editing, geometry adaptation and coherent small-scale scenes.
projects.boundary: A product reference; no embeddable library or source licence established by this review.

projects.name: Dystopika
projects.summary: A cyberpunk city-building sandbox focused on arranging a skyline and atmosphere.
projects.study: Large-scale silhouettes, night lighting and a low-friction creative interface.
projects.boundary: Visual and interaction inspiration, not a documented reusable city-generation API.

projects.name: Bulwark: Falconeer Chronicles
projects.summary: A building-focused game combining settlements with exploration and strategic interaction.
projects.study: Connected structures, vertical settlements and building across difficult terrain.
projects.boundary: Broader gameplay than a no-goal building toy. Included as product inspiration, not reusable source.

projects.name: Cloud Gardens
projects.summary: Small scenes of urban decay are transformed by growing vegetation and placing objects.
projects.study: Plant-filled dioramas, composition and environmental storytelling.
projects.boundary: Game behaviour does not establish a reusable botany model or biological realism.

projects.name: SUMMERHOUSE
projects.summary: A small creative building game for composing inhabited-looking places.
projects.study: Restrained interface, authored details and small scene composition.
projects.boundary: Adjacent creative-editor inspiration. A procedural implementation is NOT established merely because the game resembles other building toys.

projects.name: Bad North
projects.summary: A tactical game featuring procedurally generated islands.
projects.study: Readable small islands and terrain that supports gameplay constraints.
projects.boundary: A combat game, not a city editor; no reusable generation library established here.

projects.name: Irregular Grid
projects.summary: Browser experiments exploring irregular grids, mesh structure and Townscaper-like construction techniques.
projects.study: The closest practical starting point in this collection for studying organic grids and mesh generation.
projects.boundary: Educational experiments, not a production town-building engine. Integration and output quality need testing.

license.note: Review bundled examples and dependencies independently.

projects.name: HexagridRelaxing
projects.summary: A C++ grid-generation and relaxation experiment inspired by Oskar Stalberg's work.
projects.study: Native grid relaxation and irregular topology.
projects.boundary: A prototype, not a town generator. No clear source licence was established; do not assume reuse permission.

license.note: Source visibility alone is not an open-source licence.

projects.name: TownBuilder
projects.summary: An educational attempt to recreate aspects of Townscaper's procedural construction.
projects.study: Decomposing the building toy into implementable experiments.
projects.boundary: Unofficial educational reproduction. A reusable engine and clear source licence were not established.

license.note: Resolve licensing before copying implementation or assets.

projects.name: Organic Grid Townscaper
projects.summary: Python code that generates organic irregular grids inspired by Townscaper.
projects.study: A small topology prototype before integrating geometry into a renderer.
projects.boundary: Generates grids, not finished architecture or a whole game.

license.note: Code licence does not automatically cover all dependencies or third-party assets.

projects.name: WaveFunctionCollapse
projects.summary: Pattern and tile synthesis using local compatibility constraints.
projects.study: How examples and adjacency rules can drive coherent procedural outputs.
projects.boundary: A solver is not a complete city renderer. Contradictions and authored tile rules still need handling.

projects.name: WaveFunctionCollapse JavaScript
projects.summary: A JavaScript implementation exposing overlapping and tiled generation models.
projects.study: Browser integration, injectable randomness and bounded generation steps.
projects.boundary: Produces pattern/image results; 3D meshes, gameplay rules and user editing require host code.

projects.name: MarkovJunior
projects.summary: A probabilistic pattern-rewriting language with bitmap and voxel generation examples.
projects.study: Grammar-like rewriting for architecture, patterns and staged generation.
projects.boundary: A reference language and examples, not an automatically embeddable browser engine.

projects.name: DeBroglie
projects.summary: A C# constraint-based generation library supporting backtracking and additional non-local constraints.
projects.study: Generation with stronger structural requirements than simple local adjacency.
projects.boundary: Custom tile sets, constraints and rendering are still application work.

projects.name: ghx_proc_gen
projects.summary: Rust procedural generation using constraint solving, with Bevy integration examples.
projects.study: A promising Rust route for model selection, socket compatibility and generated layouts.
projects.boundary: Core code and example assets have different licences. Rust availability does not establish Swift, WASM or Apple Silicon compatibility.

license.note: README identifies CC-BY-SA-4.0 pillar/canyon assets and CC-BY-4.0 tile-layer assets.

projects.name: Watabou Medieval Fantasy City Generator
projects.summary: Stylized medieval city-map generation, with an older public source implementation in TownGeneratorOS.
projects.study: Districts, streets and city silhouettes; links from map generation to scene building.
projects.boundary: The public source is older than the live tool. Permission to use generated maps does not establish permission to reuse source code.

license.note: The live tool's author permits commercial use of generated maps; source licensing remains unresolved in this review.

projects.name: Azgaar Fantasy Map Generator
projects.summary: A browser-based generator and editor for richly structured fantasy world maps.
projects.study: Combining geography with settlements and world-building layers in an editable product.
projects.boundary: A full application rather than a minimal drop-in library; adapt selected subsystems deliberately.

license.note: The upstream licence also explicitly addresses derivative maps and other outputs; consult the complete text.

projects.name: Red Blob Games Mapgen4
projects.summary: An interactive map-generation experiment combining painted input with procedural terrain and rivers.
projects.study: Human-guided generation instead of repeatedly rolling a random seed.
projects.boundary: Stylized map generation is not a validated geophysical model. Main code and dependencies have separate terms.

license.note: The README identifies the main code licence and separately licensed dependencies.

projects.name: Infinigen
projects.summary: Procedural scene generation for detailed environments and synthetic visual data.
projects.study: Offline asset generation and the composition of many scene generators.
projects.boundary: A heavier authoring/research pipeline, not a small real-time browser world engine.

projects.name: THREE.Terrain
projects.summary: Procedural terrain generation and height-data handling for Three.js.
projects.study: A browser terrain layer that can be combined with vegetation and settlement generators.
projects.boundary: Terrain generation alone does not supply city logic, navigation or ecosystem simulation.

projects.name: EZ-Tree
projects.summary: Procedural tree-geometry generation for Three.js.
projects.study: Parameter-driven tree variation for small towns and dioramas.
projects.boundary: Tree meshes do not imply growth simulation, species ecology or resource conservation.

projects.name: proctree.js
projects.summary: A compact JavaScript procedural tree-mesh generator.
projects.study: Direct generation of branch and foliage geometry.
projects.boundary: Legacy implementation requiring compatibility review. A clear licence was not established from the reviewed material.

license.note: Unverified is not a claim that no licence exists; inspect source headers and obtain clarification before reuse.

projects.name: 2D Space Colonization Experiments
projects.summary: Interactive experiments generating branching structures through space colonization.
projects.study: Attractor-driven branching and incremental development of plant-like structures.
projects.boundary: A useful educational reference with a non-commercial restriction; not a permissively licensed commercial dependency.

license.note: NonCommercial and ShareAlike conditions are explicit in the repository licence.

projects.name: Material Maker
projects.summary: A node-based procedural material and texture authoring application built with Godot.
projects.study: Authoring repeatable surface detail for buildings, terrain and props.
projects.boundary: Desktop authoring software, not automatically a browser shader library.

projects.name: Shan, Shui
projects.summary: Procedurally generated Chinese landscape artwork rendered as SVG.
projects.study: Strong art direction built from procedural strokes and compositional rules.
projects.boundary: A stylized artwork generator, not a terrain or physics simulation.

projects.name: fishdraw
projects.summary: Procedural fish drawings with vector and structured drawing outputs.
projects.study: Anatomical variation and expressive line art without a learned image model.
projects.boundary: Generated appearance is not a swimming, behavioural or ecological simulation.

projects.name: Lenia
projects.summary: Continuous cellular automata producing organism-like evolving patterns.
projects.study: Emergent form and behaviour from local update rules.
projects.boundary: An artificial-life reference, not a complete ecology or procedural town generator.

projects.name: ALIEN
projects.summary: A GPU artificial-life environment combining particle simulation, constructed organisms and agent controllers.
projects.study: Self-organization and the relationship between physical structure and behaviour.
projects.boundary: CUDA/OpenGL requirements are a major integration constraint; no M1 Max compatibility is asserted. Some agents use neural controllers.

license.note: Current upstream README identifies BSD-3-Clause; third-party dependencies still need review.

projects.name: biosim4
projects.summary: An evolution simulator whose agents use genetically encoded neural-network brains.
projects.study: Selection, mutations and emerging behaviour in a small simulated world.
projects.boundary: Upstream describes maintenance-only development. This is evolution plus neural control, not just procedural geometry.

license.note: Licence reviewed separately from the README.
